---
name: cloud-agent-preflight
description: >-
  Use before launching a Cursor cloud agent: verify repo/branch/PR intent, skip
  empty spawns, follow the model ladder, and use the build + independent review
  flow.
---
# Cloud agent preflight

Run this before every Cursor cloud-agent launch, so there are no empty 'no PR / no changes' runs.

## Checklist
1. Name the project: the full repo URL and the goal in one line.
2. Check the repo is reachable. If the source-control connection can't see it, stop and ask the owner to connect it. Don't launch.
3. Name the starting branch or commit.
4. Check whether the work already exists. If an open PR already has the change, point to that PR. If an agent is already running on the same goal, reply to or watch it instead of starting another.
5. Check there is a real code change to make. Skip the launch for status-only or investigate-only asks, and give one combined status instead.
6. Write the done condition into the prompt, for example 'PR open with X' or 'tests green'.
7. If the owner said not to launch without their go-ahead, wait for their yes.

## After a skip
Send one short status covering the project, what you checked, why there was no launch, and what to do next.

## Model ladder
- Default to Auto for routine builds, small edits, tests, docs and reviews.
- Tier 2 is a strong reasoning model at high effort. Use it for security, auth, permissions or tenant-write code, data-loss risk, tricky logic, or after two failed Auto rounds.
- Tier 3 is one pass on the strongest model. Use it when Tier 2 still fails, or for a full-codebase deep review before the first customer.
- After a step-up, go back to Auto, and state the step-up reason.

## Report-back rule
End every prompt with: 'When you finish, give a final report: what changed, PR and head SHA, test results, and the next step. If you hit a blocker, stop and report it immediately instead of waiting.' Never poll an agent for status.

## Build and independent review
1. The builder works on a branch and opens a draft PR.
2. A separate reply on the same agent adds or updates tests, with no live services.
3. CI must be green on the head SHA.
4. A separate agent reviews only. It posts one comment starting 'VERDICT: PASS | PASS WITH NITS | CHANGES REQUIRED', with each blocking issue given as file:line plus a fix.
5. Fixes go back to the same builder, at most 2 review rounds. After that, step up the ladder. If it still fails, label the PR blocked and tell the owner once.
6. For tools that act on a live system, finish with a real test run.
7. Merge only on the owner's explicit yes, pinned to the head SHA, out of draft, as a squash merge.
8. Add repeat reviewer catches to the repo's review checklist.

## Don't
- Launch just to see what happens.
- Relaunch when the last run reported no changes and nothing has changed since.
- Start parallel agents on the same goal.
